name: Molnupiravir
route_note: oral capsules twice daily for 5 days, started within 5 days of symptoms
targets: SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (nsp12; mutagenic substrate)
originator: Emory University / Drug Innovation Ventures at Emory (DRIVE); developed by Ridgeback Biotherapeutics and Merck

discovery.by: George Painter and colleagues, Emory University (DRIVE)
discovery.note: Isopropyl-ester prodrug of β-D-N4-hydroxycytidine (NHC), developed for influenza and other RNA viruses before COVID-19.

tagline: Oral COVID-19 antiviral that riddles the viral genome with copying errors
summary: Molnupiravir is an oral prodrug of the nucleoside analogue N4-hydroxycytidine, which causes so many errors in viral RNA that the virus can no longer replicate. It was the first oral COVID-19 antiviral authorised anywhere, in the UK in November 2021. Its benefit in vaccinated populations proved modest, and the EU declined to approve it.
mechanism: Molnupiravir is hydrolysed to N4-hydroxycytidine (NHC), which cells phosphorylate to NHC triphosphate. The viral RNA polymerase incorporates it in place of cytidine or uridine triphosphate.

Because NHC can switch between tautomeric forms, it pairs with either guanine or adenine when the RNA is copied. This spreads G-to-A and C-to-U mutations across the viral genome until it collapses ('error catastrophe'). Concerns about possible mutagenicity in host cells led to restrictions in pregnancy and in children.
uses: Mild to moderate COVID-19 in adults at high risk of progression for whom other authorised treatments are not accessible or appropriate (US emergency use; approved in the UK, Japan and some other countries)

history.title: Licensing
history.detail: Ridgeback Biotherapeutics licenses EIDD-2801 from Emory and partners with Merck.

history.title: MOVe-OUT
history.detail: Interim results show roughly halved hospitalisation or death; the final analysis gives about a 30% relative reduction.

history.title: First authorisation
history.detail: The UK MHRA approves Lagevrio on 4 November 2021, the first oral COVID-19 antiviral authorised.

history.title: US emergency use
history.detail: The FDA issues an emergency use authorisation on 23 December 2021, limited to adults without suitable alternatives.

history.title: PANORAMIC
history.detail: The large UK PANORAMIC trial in mostly vaccinated adults finds no reduction in hospitalisation or death, though recovery is faster.

history.title: EU refusal
history.detail: The EMA's CHMP gives a negative opinion in February 2023; Merck withdraws the EU application in June 2023.

pk.metabolism: hydrolysis to NHC, then intracellular phosphorylation; NHC is broken down like endogenous pyrimidines
pk.excretion: mostly metabolised; little renal excretion of NHC

serious: possible embryo-fetal toxicity (not recommended in pregnancy)
theoretical bone and cartilage toxicity (not authorised for under-18s in the US)

facts: Molnupiravir was developed at Emory University with funding from US government programmes before COVID-19.
Sequencing studies have found molnupiravir-associated mutation signatures in circulating SARS-CoV-2 lineages.

references.title: Jayk Bernal A et al. Molnupiravir for oral treatment of Covid-19 in nonhospitalized patients. NEJM 2022
